subject: Hosted API response-time evidence request and temporary SLO adjustment
messages:
From: Kelsey Ramos <kelsey@bluehaven.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@bluehaven.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p50/p95 ask + onboarding window

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the team was impressed with Redwood's telemetry and the routing controls.

We have one open item before procurement will sign: Bluehaven requires a documented approach for hosted API latency commitments (p50/p95) and a path for a temporary measurement-window adjustment during our initial onboarding (first 30 days). Specifically: 
- We expect a contractual reference for p50 and p95 for the hosted API; we are open to staged commitments during onboarding.
- We want clarity on how you measure p50/p95 (sampling/windowing rules) and what evidence we can request if we believe the measurement is not representative (e.g., traffic skew from our side, large tail due to specific endpoints).

Can you share the evidence package you typically provide for temporary SLO adjustments (traffic samples, telemetry config, and sample logs)? Also, if you offer a short-term SLO relaxation during ramp, what are the guardrails and rollback criteria?

Attaching a small traffic sample from our side to help calibrate.

Thanks,
Kelsey Ramos
Director of Platform Engineering
Bluehaven Analytics
[Attachment: bluehaven-traffic-sample.csv (text/csv, 14KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Ramos <kelsey@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Oct 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p50/p95 ask + onboarding window

Kelsey — really appreciate the clear ask and the sample.

High level answers up front: yes, we can support a time-bound onboarding adjustment with an evidence package. Typical approach we propose: 
- Measurement definition: p50/p95 computed over 1-minute aggregation buckets, aggregated across a rolling 24-hour reporting window for contractual measurement; evidence for an exception uses per-hour sampling and a 14-day lookback.
- Short-term adjustment: 30-day probationary window during onboarding where p50/p95 targets are agreed in writing and monitored; we require a 72-hour canary (low-traffic) followed by full traffic monitoring.
- Guardrails: temporary adjustment limited to the specific routes in-scope; auto-fallback to an agreed model variant if p95 exceeds threshold for >=3 consecutive 1-hour epochs.

I've attached our SLO evidence template and a mutual-action-plan draft that outlines roles, data we request, and acceptable proof artifacts. Karthik I've looped you in to propose concrete numbers (we can be prescriptive by route or provide a regional uplift).

Next steps: could you confirm the routes/endpoints you're most concerned about and share the Prod key for a read-only telemetry export (or grant access to a Redash/Looker view)? Once we have that, we can produce the evidence package within 3 business days.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-evidence-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)]

From: Kelsey Ramos <kelsey@bluehaven.ai>
To: Grace O'Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@bluehaven.ai>, Procurement <procurement@bluehaven.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API p50/p95 ask + onboarding window

Grace — thanks. We care about two high-volume endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. We can grant a read-only API key to a telemetry export (I'll send to the address you prefer).

For numbers, our internal baseline is p50 ~ 95ms and p95 ~ 420ms on our dev traffic; during ramp we can tolerate a temporary delta but procurement wants explicit rollback triggers.

I've attached the CSV I mentioned (same file referenced above) and a short note from our SRE on peak patterns.

—Kelsey
[Attachment: bluehaven-traffic-sample.csv (text/csv, 14KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: internal: proposed contract language and thresholds

Grace / Marissa — drafting suggested terms for our reply to Bluehaven. Key points I recommend we propose: 
1) Contractual measurement: p50/p95 reported as daily aggregated percentiles computed from 1-minute latency buckets across the hosted region; reporting window for SLA compliance is the calendar day.
2) Onboarding adjustment: 30-calendar-day probation where customer and Redwood agree to adjusted targets for specified routes (we should keep this per-route). During probation we will: 72-hour canary (10% of traffic), then ramp to full.
3) Specific numbers (proposal):
   - Baseline commitment after probation: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 480ms (US region, hosted).
   - Probationary (temporary) targets: p50 <= 170ms, p95 <= 700ms for the 30-day window, provided evidence of application-side traffic shaping.
4) Rollback & remediation: automated fallback to regional lower-latency model variant if p95 > probationary threshold for 3 consecutive 1-hour epochs; customer can trigger an audit request with 48-hour notice.
5) Evidence we will accept: sampled traces (first/last token timings), server-side percentiles by route (CSV), and the customer's traffic sample; we will produce an evidence bundle and a short findings memo.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-v1.docx (MVP) with milestones, owner assignments, and DocuSign-ready clause for provisional targets.

If Marissa signs off I can send this back to Bluehaven and open a HubSpot task for the follow-up.

—Karthik
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 12KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Ramos <kelsey@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API response-time evidence request and temporary SLO adjustment

Kelsey — thanks for the quick turn. We've reviewed the sample and discussed internally. Summary of agreed next steps: 

1) Agreement in principle:
   - Redwood to provide a 30-calendar-day probationary window for the two routes (/v1/generate, /v1/embeddings) with provisional targets p50 <= 170ms and p95 <= 700ms while we monitor ramp behavior.
   - Post-probation contractual commitment (subject to evidence): p50 <= 120ms and p95 <= 480ms (US hosted region).

2) Canary & monitoring:
   - 72-hour canary at 10% traffic, then 4x ramp steps over 48 hours to full traffic; Redwood provides a daily findings memo during the probation.

3) Rollback / audit:
   - Automated fallback if p95 exceeds provisional threshold for 3 consecutive 1-hour epochs.
   - Bluehaven may request an audit; Redwood will assemble the evidence bundle within 72 hours of request.

4) Next logistics:
   - Please send a read-only telemetry credential to telemetry+bluehaven@redwood.ai and we'll produce the evidence package within 3 business days.
   - I'll also attach the mutual action plan and a DocuSign link for the provisional SLO clause; procurement can sign that to lock the probation window.

I've attached the SLO evidence template and the mutual action plan for your review. If that looks good I'll route the DocuSign envelope to your procurement contact.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-evidence-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)]
